appearance_facts.fact: Vertical color legend runs from a pale yellow/white top labeled '100 Low' to a deep maroon bottom labeled '0 High'. Intermediate tick labels read 80, 60, 40, 20. The color scale is inverted relative to typical heatmaps: darker red/maroon corresponds to higher prevalence (0 High), while pale yellow corresponds to lower prevalence (100 Low).
Title text reads 'Prevalence of Species Z in Each State'.
Each state is filled with a solid color from the legend scale and labeled with its two-letter postal abbreviation. States with no data (e.g., CA, AZ, NM, CO, UT, AR, AL, RI) are filled light gray.
Filled with the darkest maroon color on the map, matching the '0 High' end of the legend. The label 'NY' is printed in white text inside the state polygon.
Filled with a pale yellow color, matching the '100 Low' end of the legend. The label 'NC' is printed in black text inside the state polygon.
Filled with an orange color, matching the mid-range of the legend (approximately 40-60). The label 'DE' is printed in black text inside the state polygon.
NY is visibly darker (higher prevalence) than DE, which is darker than NC. NY is among the darkest states on the map, alongside IL, KY, OH, WA, and MT.

printed_facts.fact: Top tick: '100 Low'. Bottom tick: '0 High'. Intermediate ticks: 80, 60, 40, 20. Color gradient: pale yellow (top) to deep maroon (bottom).
NY (New York) is labeled in white text. NC (North Carolina) is labeled in black text. DE (Delaware) is labeled in black text.
'Prevalence of Species Z in Each State'

public_definitions: Routing criterion: 'Highest prevalence state in the dashboard'
Option condition: Select the state with the highest prevalence (darkest color on the inverted scale) for priority follow-up routing.
uncertain: Exact numerical prevalence values are not printed on the map; only the color scale is provided. The determination of 'highest' relies on visual color matching to the legend's '0 High' end.

Several states (IL, KY, OH, WA, MT, TX, GA) appear to share a similar dark red/maroon color. NY is among the darkest, but precise ranking between these dark states cannot be determined without numerical data.
